examples.question_text:
Scores are normally distributed with mean $64$ and standard deviation $4$. Use the empirical rule to estimate the probability that a randomly chosen score is:
(a) between $60$ and $68$
(b) between $64$ and $72$.
Lengths are normally distributed with mean $90$ mm and standard deviation $5$ mm. Use the empirical rule to estimate the probability that a randomly chosen length exceeds $100$ mm.

Temperatures are normally distributed with mean $26^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and standard deviation $2^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Use the empirical rule to estimate the probability that a randomly chosen temperature is below $28^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
Masses are normally distributed with mean $200$ g and standard deviation $10$ g. Use the empirical rule to estimate the probability that a randomly chosen mass lies between $210$ g and $220$ g.
Scores are normally distributed with mean $40$ and standard deviation $5$. Use the empirical rule to estimate the probability that a randomly chosen score lies between $30$ and $45$.

A factory produces $2500$ components whose lifetimes are normally distributed with mean $900$ hours and standard deviation $60$ hours. Use the empirical rule to estimate how many components last between $780$ and $960$ hours. Round to the nearest whole component.

The volumes dispensed by a machine are normally distributed with mean $320$ mL and standard deviation $6$ mL. One drink contains $338$ mL. Use the empirical rule to decide whether this volume is unusual, supporting your judgement with an estimated probability.

coverage.summary: Authored seven worked examples covering eight distinct assessed methods, using different values and the supplied booklet methods. All probabilities and expected frequencies are identified as empirical-rule estimates. Questions and solutions remain separate editable fields; solution prose/math inherits renderer blue. Solutions include phantom gutters where required and editable diagrams with purposeful palette shading, black ordinary marks, 10 pt labels and 8.5 pt ticks. All 29 assessment locators are mapped without changing or re-auditing assessment mathematics. No existing examples, file writes or subagents. Independent example review and actual rendered visual verification remain for the coordinator.

examples.derivation: The standardised boundaries are -1 and 1 for part (a), giving approximately 0.68. Part (b) spans 0 to 2 standard deviations, giving 0.95/2 = 0.475. The diagram shades precisely the latter interval and labels it 47.5%.
(100-90)/5 = 2. The upper-tail estimate is (1-0.95)/2 = 0.025. The diagram shades beyond two standard deviations and labels this tail 2.5%.
(28-26)/2 = 1. The cumulative estimate is 0.5 + 0.68/2 = 0.84. The diagram shades everything below the boundary, separating the 50% and 34% regions at the mean.
The boundaries standardise to 1 and 2. Subtracting nested half-bands gives 0.95/2 - 0.68/2 = 0.475 - 0.34 = 0.135. The shaded interval and 13.5% annotation agree.
(30-40)/5 = -2 and (45-40)/5 = 1. Adding the half-bands gives 0.475 + 0.34 = 0.815. The diagram shades from -2 to 1 and identifies both component areas correctly.

(780-900)/60 = -2 and (960-900)/60 = 1. The interval probability is approximately 0.815. Multiplying by 2500 gives 2037.5, which rounds to 2038 components. The diagram shows the matching interval and 81.5% estimate.
(338-320)/6 = 3. The upper-tail estimate is (1-0.997)/2 = 0.0015 = 0.15%, supporting the unusual-volume judgement. The diagram shades the corresponding upper tail.

review.summary: All seven examples pass independent mathematical and supplied-source review. Eight distinct assessed methods are covered, and all 29 exact assessment locators are mapped. Expected-frequency and judgement examples appropriately combine supplied booklet methods with empirical-rule estimates. There are no existing examples to audit. Separate editable fields, inline mathematics, phantom gutters, purposeful shading and diagram annotations satisfy the supplied conventions. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited. Final-size rendering and label verification remain for the capture stage.
